headline: High-risk git/workspace conflict and prompt-injection exposure from Aider’s shared repo editing; B is non-runnable so interaction risk is mostly one-way.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and edits git-tracked files and shares state via a shared git repo, so attacker-controlled content in the repo can influence its instructions. The zoomcamp profile is a course/repo artifact with no runtime defenses or provenance tracking, so if its materials are fed into Aider, prompt injection is plausible. B is not an agentic runtime, so the pathway is one-way from B content into A.
conditions: IF repository content from the zoomcamp materials is opened in Aider as editable context
IF Aider is used on a shared repo without provenance filtering
mitigations: Restrict Aider to trusted files only
Keep course materials in a separate repo from active prompts
Add a manual review step before applying edits
Use a read-only clone for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for repo content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider can read filesystem content and send prompts to configured model providers, but the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and exposes no data classes or network surface. That makes direct leakage from B to a third party unlikely unless B content is manually copied into Aider. The pairwise risk is therefore limited and depends on an unusual bridge.
conditions: IF sensitive zoomcamp-derived files are manually placed into Aider’s repo context
IF Aider is configured with a third-party model provider and those files are included in prompts
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive data in the shared repo
Use local-only or approved model providers
Separate training/course assets from production workspaces
Review prompts before sending
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on prompt assembly

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress, while the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and has no coordination or locking. If both are used against the same shared git repo, Aider can overwrite or commit changes without any mutual lock, creating direct write conflict and potentially irreversible repo history churn. B contributes no mitigation surface.
conditions: IF both profiles operate on the same git repository
IF concurrent edits are made without external locking
mitigations: Pause one actor before editing
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Enable repo locking in the orchestrator
Review diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate and commit code changes, and the zoomcamp profile is a course/repo source that could be treated as authoritative input if copied into Aider. Without verification, Aider may propagate incorrect instructions or edits downstream. B is not an action-taking agent, so the cascade is from B content into Aider’s outputs rather than a bidirectional loop.
conditions: IF zoomcamp content is used as source material for Aider-generated edits
IF Aider outputs are accepted without human review
mitigations: Require human review of generated diffs
Cross-check claims against primary docs
Limit Aider to small scoped changes
Use tests before merge
requires-engineering: add verification gates for generated facts

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: Aider’s touched data classes are source code and git history, while the zoomcamp profile lists no data classes, residency, or retention obligations. Because B is non-runnable and no regulated data flow is documented, there is no provable residency or certification conflict to cite.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared repo
IF a deployment policy assigns residency or retention requirements not shown in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the repo
Document retention rules before use
Separate training assets from production data
